terra.problem: The joke says Jacob put up a sign. The text says he named the place, not that he made a sign.
The explanation is mechanical and repetitive: it states that the message uses servant, then restates it without adding much.
Jacob says he sent the message so he might find favor. The message does not say he asks Esau for favor.
Calling it a tricky one comments on the question itself.
The passage does not say that nobody is lining up for battle. It says Jacob divides his people and animals into camps.
Comparing the threatened camps to cookies in boxes makes light of a possible attack on people.
The explanation invents a reason Jacob chose to repeat this promise: that its countless sand image was why he picked it.
The gift-card joke puts a modern object into the Bible scene, and the comparison does not match Jacob's action of selecting a gift.
The explanation suggests a purpose for spacing the herds: getting Esau to meet them one at a time. The text does not give that reason.
Jacob instructed the servant; the passage does not say he wrote the lines. It also does not establish here that Esau actually hears them.
Genesis 32:4 says Jacob stayed with Laban, but does not establish that Laban was his relative. That fact needs a supporting reference from elsewhere.
Saying a sure man would not need a parade of herds adds an unsupported claim about why Jacob arranged the gift that way.
